evidence_excerpts: When faced with a case in which it seems that [p] is fully grounded in D yet ~䊐(∧D → p), the advocate of necessity should check to see if there are additional explanatorily relevant facts P such that 䊐(∧(D, P) → p).
text: Apparent counterexamples to grounding necessity fail either because they mistake merely partial grounds for full grounds or because they mistake a non-ground for a ground.
